steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease 12 muffin cups or line with paper muffin liners.
Whisk together milk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla in a medium bowl until well combined.

Mix together flour, oats, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, pumpkin pie spice, and salt in a large bowl until well combined. Make a well in the center and pour in egg mixture. Stir until just combined. Gently fold in blackberries. Divide batter evenly into the prepared muffin cups and sprinkle the tops with turbinado sugar.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of a muffin comes out clean, about 20 minutes. Cool muffins in the pan for 10 minutes before removing to cool completely on a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Blackberry Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Pumpkin pie spice makes these blackberry muffins special and comforting, and with just a bit of butter, you can feel good about this breakfast treat.

review.reviewBody: After reading reviews (dry muffins)and having made muffins with oats as an ingredient (DRY) I made these with the following modifications and they came out very moist and delicious. I cut the oats to 1/2 a cup and added 3/4 a cup more of fresh blackberries and 1/2 cup mini chocolate chips. Baking time was 17 min in my oven. YUMMY!

My first time making blackberry muffins & using this recipe. Yummy! Moist, flavorful & satisfying! I doubled the recipe & added 1 t almond extract (just because I like almond flavor with berries), in addition to the required vanilla. It made 24 mini & 18 regular muffins. I started breaking the fresh berries in half after mixing it all together since I was filling mini ones. I wanted to be sure every muffin got some berry in it. It worked very well!

These were tasty! After reading several reviews, I decided to make some changes to make them less dense. I substituted 1/2 cup oil for the butter, cut the oatmeal to 1/2 cup and put it in a grinder, and I added one very ripe banana and a few more blackberries. I would definitely make these again.

Based on the reviews I made a couple of substitutions. I substituted 1/2 c of the oatmeal for 1/4 c of wheat germ & 1/4 c of flax meal. I also subbed 1c of wheat flour instead for 1 c of all-purpose. Since some of the reviews stated that the mixture was on the thick side I decided to add 1/2 c of orange juice to the batter and I also increased the pumpkin pie spice to 1 tsp. Glad I made these changes. These were definitely yummy and I got about 18 nice sized muffins. A keeper with the changes I made.
After reading the reviews, I used 2 eggs and 3 tbsp more brown sugar. I used 2 cups blackberries and subbed sour cream for the milk. I will make again. Moist but not sweet enough.

I used thawed blackberries, whole wheat pastry flour, and doubled the pumpkin pie seasoning...they all worked great. Based on the reviews that said the muffins were dry, I made my own modifications. I used hot water in place of milk, quick oats in place of rolled, and grapeseed oil in place of butter. My muffins turned out flavorful and moist...I will make these again soon! Another reviewer suggested adding some chocolate chips...I did, because who doesn't like chocolate chips? I won't add chocolate chips to these again...they detracted from the blackberries which were great on their own.

I made half the recipe and used blueberries as suggested by the recipe submitter. I added butter and a bit of flour to the turbinado sugar for the topping, resulting in a streusel-like topping. They were tasty but a bit on the dense side. Thank you for sharing your recipe.

This recipe is yummy. I added chocolate chips. I didnt use pumpkin pie spice. I used cinnamon instead. I have regular sized cupcake tins and this recipe made 24 muffins. I baked the first pan for 20 minutes and they were over baked on the bottoms. The next pan I baked for 15 minutes and that was perfect. They taste better cold from the refrigerator.

Taking into consideration all of the comments about dryness and density, these are the changes I made: 1 cup buttermilk instead of milk, 1/4 cup cooking oil for the butter and 2 eggs instead of one. I used 3/4 cup oatmeal and whole wheat flour. For the spices I added 1/2 tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp salt and added cinnamon chips. It made 28 muffins that were moist and delicious!
Loved them. I used cinnamon instead of the pumpkin spice and instead of the 1/4 cup of sugar I used molasses they were perfect and not to sweet, also sprinkled sugar on the top before baking

Very good, whole family liked these better than traditional muffins. I omitted the pumpkin pie spice as I did not have any on hand, but will try it next time.
I also used mixed berries (raspberries, blueberries, strawberries, blackberries).

These muffins are so good! They are nice and crunchy on the outside and perfectly moist inside. They're not overly sweet and the bites with blackberries add a sweet/tart punch. I used gluten free flour and cut my blackberries in half (they wre huge). I will be making these again!

I did not have brown sugar so replaced it equally with cane sugar, came out very sweet and delicious. also substituted 1 tbsp butter for avocado oil.. I also wanted a more complex texture, and replaced 1 cup of flour with 1/2 cup almond flour and 2 tbsp coconut flour… the measurements weren’t exact but i know what the texture of muffin mix should get to. so with these modifications, the muffins were delicious:)
Relish as written
Best berry muffins I've ever made - and for my taste, the best muffins! Slightly crispy-crunchy on top, super moist and delicious inside. I've already made two double batches and everyone loves them.
Delicious, but sticks to muffin wrappers so bad that half the muffin is lost I’ve made this recipe a few times and it’s happened every time
I made it into a loaf bread. Set temp. to 375 and baked 45 min to an hour
I didn't have pumpkin pie spice, so I used nutmeg. They turned out very yummy!!
Yum! I followed Karen1234’s recipe but I think even less time might be warranted. Made 20 muffins.
Great tasting muffins. I added a little oat bran =)
